title: MDK12-Bench: A Comprehensive Evaluation of Multimodal Large Language Models on Multidisciplinary Exams
extended_summary:
This paper addresses the problem of how to rigorously evaluate multimodal large language models (MLLMs) on educational problem-solving tasks, especially in ways that go beyond static benchmarks. The authors argue that existing multimodal exams are too small, too narrow, and too weakly annotated to reveal how models perform across difficulty levels, changing exam years, and different question formats.

To address this, the paper introduces MDK12-Bench, a large benchmark built from real-world K–12 exams across six disciplines: mathematics, physics, chemistry, biology, geography, and information science. The benchmark includes 141K instances, five question formats, difficulty labels, exam-year annotations, a six-layer knowledge taxonomy, and detailed explanations. The authors also propose a dynamic evaluation framework that perturbs visual and textual inputs, and they test knowledge-point reference-augmented generation (KP-RAG) to examine whether explicit knowledge references improve reasoning.

The population represented is K–12 educational content rather than human participants: the benchmark spans elementary, middle school, and high school material, and the data curation process involved researchers and K–12 educators. The context is benchmark development and model evaluation rather than classroom implementation. The main conclusions are that current MLLMs perform better on easier and older items, struggle more with math and physics, are highly sensitive to contextual shifts, and gain only limited benefit from knowledge augmentation on harder reasoning tasks. The paper concludes that more robust, generalizable multimodal models require better reasoning, multimodal fusion, and knowledge integration.

identified_tools.name: GenAI (General)
identified_tools.description: Multimodal large language models (MLLMs): AI systems that combine language and visual inputs to solve problems, generate answers, and perform reasoning across text-image tasks.
identified_tools.use_case: The paper benchmarks a range of MLLMs on real-world K–12 multidisciplinary exam questions, including standard, dynamic, and knowledge-point reference-augmented (KP-RAG) evaluation settings. It evaluates proprietary and open-source models rather than a single product.

findings.finding_summary: Across 141,320 K–12 exam instances, current MLLMs showed substantial limitations in multidisciplinary problem solving, especially on harder and newer exams. The paper reports accuracy drops of 8.3% on harder exams, 12.6% on newer exams, and a 13.7% average performance reduction under dynamic perturbations, indicating weak generalization and sensitivity to contextual shifts.
findings.measure: Accuracy on K–12 multidisciplinary exam questions under standard, harder/newer exam, and dynamic evaluation conditions
findings.effect_size: 13.7% performance reduction under dynamic evaluation; 8.3% drop on harder exams; 12.6% drop on newer exams

quality_tier_rationale: This is an empirical benchmark study with systematic evaluation, but it is not a classroom intervention study and does not use an experimental educational design. The evidence is quantitative and comparative, yet centered on model performance rather than learner outcomes.
impact_tier_rationale: The reported effects are notable for model robustness and generalization, but they are not direct student-impact estimates. The paper shows meaningful limitations and risks for classroom use, but no direct evidence of academic gains or harms for K-12 students.
